speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have had a fever and altered mental status for two days; to start our evaluation, are you currently experiencing any stiff neck, severe headache, or light sensitivity?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The patient's history of haloperidol use for tics, combined with fever and altered mentation while explicitly denying a stiff neck (which can occur in early stages or be absent in some presentations of NMS), makes this the primary differential. I will confirm this by checking for autonomic instability and creatine kinase levels.
